title: Elastic headroom routing and overload shedder for Dedicated pools
creator: Ayesha Kapoor
description:
Problem statement: Dedicated pools occasionally hit transient overloads when traffic patterns change (hotspots, sudden bursty fan-out from customers, or noisy neighbors). Current admission behavior is coarse: requests are either queued until queue depth cap or rejected. We need an elastic headroom routing and overload shedding system that preserves latency SLOs for latency-sensitive tiers, enforces per-tenant throughput guarantees, and provides predictable degradation modes for best-effort traffic.

Goals: implement a routing layer that tracks pool headroom and per-tenant usage, provides admission decisions based on configurable SLAs (guaranteed throughput, burst credits, priority classes), and supports multiple shedding strategies (priority-based drop, oldest-first, model-fallback to smaller quantized variant, graceful 503/Retry-After). Must integrate with Dedicated autoscaler signals so admission reacts correctly to scaling events and avoid oscillation.

Non-goals: replacing global rate-limiter library, implementing tenant billing changes, or reworking the autoscaler core algorithms (only integration hooks).
acceptance_criteria: Admission decisions can be made within 500µs median latency for a routing decision path
Under simulated 3x sudden traffic spike, guaranteed-tier customers maintain 95th percentile token latency within SLO (configurable per-pool)
Best-effort traffic is shed according to configured policy and shedding events are recorded as metrics and traces
Integration tests that simulate autoscaler scale-up/scale-down while headroom is being consumed show no cascade of failed requests beyond a bounded window (<= 10s)
Dashboard: per-pool headroom, shed events, per-tenant admission rejections, and effective throughput visible in Console
Safe default policies (conservative headroom, per-tenant burst credits) documented and enabled for existing Dedicated customers after opt-in process
design_notes: Use a hybrid token-bucket + reactive headroom estimator: token buckets track long-term guarantees, headroom estimator tracks instantaneous GPU queue depth and KV cache hotness
Admission points: API edge (fast path) for quick rejects, and internal router for advanced decisions with more context (route history, per-tenant priority)
Support three shedding modes: DROP (immediate reject), DEGRADE (route to smaller quantized model variant), and QUEUE (controlled enqueue with timeout and position-based priority)
Circuit-breaker thresholds are based on %GPU-util and p99 per-token latency windows; thresholds are configurable per-pool and per-tier
Autoscaler integration: expose headroom metric and a short-lived demand signal; ensure admission reduces load during scale-in to avoid dropped in-flight work
decisions: Default shedding policy will be priority-aware drop with a small proportion of requests diverted to DEGRADE mode for best-effort customers
Admission logic will run in the request path with a sub-1ms budget; heavier scoring runs in a fast async evaluation used for telemetry and future ML-based admission
Per-tenant burst credit model chosen over strict per-second rate limits to allow short bursts without violating guarantees
We will expose a per-pool config that maps priority classes to shedding order and to fallback model variants

Autoscaler: add headroom telemetry export and short-lived demand signal (ENG-16101.3)
Runtime: implement degrade routing to quantized model variants and ensure KV cache consistency (ENG-16101.4)
Testing: end-to-end chaos tests for burst+scale scenarios and unit tests for token-bucket correctness (ENG-16101.5)
Console: dashboard tiles and runbook links for shed events (ENG-16101.6)
Docs: update Dedicated runbook and customer-facing guide with default policies and opt-in instructions (ENG-16101.7)
